fieldMarks: Medium lizard, 5-7 in, with smooth shiny scales and short legs; back olive-gray to brown.
Wide dark brown or black lateral stripe from head onto tail, edged above and below by a thin light line; belly gray or bluish-gray.
No stripe down the centre of the back (the common and southeastern five-lined skinks have one).
Breeding males have an orange or reddish tint on the sides of the head; females slightly larger.
behavior: Courtship and breeding in spring (late winter in Georgia); females lay 4-9 eggs in rotten logs or moist soil and guard them.
Sheds its tail if grasped; active March-September in Kansas and all year in Georgia; often shelters under logs and rocks near water and may take refuge in water.
habitat: Open, moist forests near streams, rivers or sloughs, also rocky hillsides and near springs; humid wooded areas with leaf litter and loose rocks, sometimes clearcuts and rights-of-way.
range: Only the Tennessee range was sourced: a southern coal skink subspecies along the Tennessee River in the west and a northern one in Great Smoky Mountains National Park.
